I encouraged Johnny to view EasyPay as a sales tool rather than waiting for customers to ask about financing. I explained that many customers may assume they cannot afford recommended repairs, but by offering financing, they may discover they qualify and can move forward with work they otherwise would have postponed. Positioning financing early in the conversation can help increase repair orders while providing customers with an affordable payment option.

Johnny appreciated the suggestion and was receptive to using financing more proactively during customer interactions.

Subject: 00UTO00000cSRfR2AW
Full Comments:
Checked in via Maps Application 
Met with the manager’s son (I didn’t catch his name) and Service Advisor Rob. The manager’s son shared that his dad is very old-school and prefers to keep things simple. They are very loyal to Snap and are not actively looking to add more financing options. He explained that his dad’s mindset is, “If it’s not broken, don’t fix it,” so introducing a new program may be challenging. He did say he would put in a good word for me with his dad.

Rob was very receptive and familiar with EasyPay from his previous experience at Fletcher’s. He shared that he plans to speak with the owner on my behalf because he believes customers benefit from having multiple financing options. He mentioned he is not a big fan of relying only on Snap and likes that EasyPay allows customers to leave without paying anything upfront. He also pointed out that while Snap advertises “zero down” with their in-store POP, customers often still have to pay something at the time of purchase...

Subject: 00UTO00000cRwzi2AC
Full Comments:
Checked in via Maps Application 
Spoke with Sabrina, the manager. After several months of follow-up visits encouraging the shop to use EasyPay again, they are finally back on board and are now running EasyPay first. They are once again producing the same level of business they did with us when we were RIC, which is a great win.

This is a good example of how consistent relationship-building and periodic follow-up can help re-engage inactive merchants over time.

Sabrina shared that overall business has been slower, but higher repair costs have resulted in larger average ticket sizes, helping offset the decrease in car count. Based on their current activity, I estimate they have the potential to fund approximately $8K–$10K with EasyPay each month.

The shop is currently on a $20 spiff. Sabrina requested a poster, which I will provide once they are back in stock. I reminded her to reach out to Connor or me if she needs any assistance.

Full Comments:
Spoke with Rob regarding the situation where an application was completed, marked as delivered, and used to obtain funding so parts could be ordered before the repairs were completed. He explained that this involved a specific customer who wanted to secure approval but keep the vehicle until the required parts arrived. Because he could not release the vehicle without ordering the parts, he marked the deal as delivered to receive funding.

I reminded Rob that this is not the correct process. The proper procedure is to obtain approval, complete all repairs on the vehicle, and only then mark the application as delivered once the work has been completed. Applications should not be marked as delivered at any point prior to the completion of repairs. Rob acknowledged the issue and stated that he will not do this again moving forward.

He mentioned that he loves our EasyPay pens, so I left him with additional promotional items. I thanked him for their continued use of EasyPay and reminded him that I’m always available if the team needs anything.

Full Comments:
Completed LTO training with David. During the training, I clearly communicated that we are not allowed to ship accessories, merchandise, or any other products. I also explained that the lease-to-own program is only available to Florida residents and that a valid government-issued ID must be verified in person.

I further advised David that this is a lease agreement and is therefore tax-exempt. As a result, no taxes should be added to the invoice.

David advised that they work with Verizon as a third-party provider. He also mentioned that they offer in-house credit and an additional loan option; however, he did not specify the lenders associated with those financing programs.

Subject: 00TTO000010RLkx2AG
Full Comments:
Called and spoke with Joanna to follow up on their most recent funded application. She mentioned that the overall process was straightforward and easy, but she was initially confused about the sales tax. She had expected the taxes to be included in the funded amount.

I clarified that EasyPay collects sales tax directly from the customer, so the merchant does not need to collect it, and explained that I would be sending over the resale certificate, which serves as documentation allowing them to avoid paying sales tax on that specific transaction.
